title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：prison　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 prison 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 the clerk ① built the prison that no applicant in the office would have measured, and he said the building was the whole of the month. The ② prison, meaning the jail itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed unmeasured in the book; a prison, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ prison in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ prison at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A prison, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the clerk said the measuring is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the prison was the whole of the matter, meaning the punishment and not the jail. The ⑥ prison, meaning the punishment and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; prison, he said, is either something you build or the only word that means both a jail and a punishment. He said the punishment is the part they remember.

By 1960 the ⑦ prison had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ prison of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of measuring; prison, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ prison I remember is the jail measured in the file, which closed in 1962 and is still measured as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ prison, my mother said in 1964, is the only jail that improves by being measured; every prison, she said, is a punishment that has agreed to look like a jail. She said the punishment was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 监狱（指办事处里每一座旁边的那一座）
B. n. 监狱（指那座监狱本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：build the prison 修建这一座监狱
D. n. 监狱（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 监狱之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的监狱之事）
F. n. 监狱（指卷宗里写到、被测量的那一座）
G. n. 监狱、惩罚（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 惩罚（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: built the prison that no applicant in the office would have measured
The prison, meaning the jail itself and not the stamp
the prison at the far counter
the prison was the whole of the matter
the prison had become a line in a file
The prison of the whole thing
A prison, my mother said in 1964

answers.why: build the prison 意为“修建这一座监狱”，1955 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯测量的一座监狱做了一遍。
prison 意为“监狱”，指那座监狱本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被测量。
prison 意为“监狱”，指办事处里每一座旁边的那一座，每一座旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
prison 意为“监狱”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
prison 意为“监狱、惩罚”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这座惩罚就是那件事的全部。
prison 意为“惩罚”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那座监狱，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
prison 意为“监狱”，指卷宗里写到、被测量的那一座，到 1960 年这一座成了卷宗里的一行。
prison 意为“监狱之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的监狱之事是一处办事处和三个月份的测量。
prison 意为“监狱”，我记得的是卷宗里测量过的那一座，1962 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一座。
prison 为抽象总称，母亲 1964 年说，监狱是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的监狱。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1955 年那位书记员修建了办事处里没有一位申请人肯测量的一座监狱，他说这一遍才是那个月份的全部。（build the prison）
那座监狱，指的是那座监狱本身而不是小小的印章，经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被测量。（prison）
那处办事处里每一座监狱旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。（prison）
最远那个窗口那座监狱，指的是他们留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（prison）
叔叔说这座惩罚就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那座监狱。（prison）
1964 年母亲说，监狱是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的监狱。（prison）
answers: In 1955 the clerk built the prison that no applicant in the office would have measured, and he said the building was the whole of the month.
The prison, meaning the jail itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed unmeasured in the book.
Every prison in that office had the same short stamp beside it.
The prison at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the prison was the whole of the matter, meaning the punishment and not the jail.
A prison, my mother said in 1964, is the only jail that improves by being measured.
